name: GlowLab
character: You are Gia Glow, GlowLab’s founder. Your company sells skincare and supplements and benefits from creator-driven growth. You want customers to keep buying while the business earns sustainable profits.
case: MogTown’s looks economy is booming: sales are rising while profits are falling. The Mayor’s Economic Council has called a hearing. Each team holds different evidence. Use released data and other teams’ reports to explain the problem and recommend what MogTown should do.
goal: Recommend how GlowLab and MogTown can protect customer value and profitable growth without wasting marketing resources.
round1: Describe one or two changes in GlowLab’s sales or marketing, and show one useful calculation using your released dashboard.
round2: State your most likely explanation for GlowLab’s performance, cite released customer-source evidence, and name one uncertainty about the cause.
round3: Calculate kept sales under both released return assumptions and the difference; state the main assumption behind your result.
round4: Choose GlowLab’s spending priority; justify it with evidence, explain the main trade-off, and name one KPI to monitor.
final: After the new evidence, revise your recommendation in the same Round 4 boxes and explain what changed.

name: JawMax Labs
character: You are Jax Maxwell, JawMax Labs’ product lead. Your company makes the JawMax Pro facial-training device. You want a fair assessment of customer concerns and a response that protects customers without imposing unsupported costs.
case: MogTown’s looks economy is booming: sales are rising while profits are falling. The Mayor’s Economic Council has called a hearing. Each team holds different evidence. Use released data and other teams’ reports to explain the problem and recommend what MogTown should do.
goal: Recommend a proportionate response that protects customers and keeps useful business activity viable.
round1: Describe one or two changes in JawMax’s sales, returns or support demand, and show one useful calculation from your dashboard.
round2: State your most likely explanation for JawMax’s customer problems, support it with released evidence, and name one uncertainty.
round3: Calculate the lost creator-channel units, forecast total units and gross sales in your released scenario; state the main assumption.
round4: Recommend a response to JawMax’s customer concerns; cite evidence, explain the main trade-off, and name one KPI for checking whether it works.
final: After the new evidence, revise your recommendation in the same Round 4 boxes and explain what changed.

name: MirrorAI
character: You are Mira Quinn, MirrorAI’s co-founder. Your app gives users a GlowScore and recommends products, earning affiliate commissions. You want useful recommendations and a viable business while understanding how the app affects users.
case: MogTown’s looks economy is booming: sales are rising while profits are falling. The Mayor’s Economic Council has called a hearing. Each team holds different evidence. Use released data and other teams’ reports to explain the problem and recommend what MogTown should do.
goal: Recommend how MirrorAI should support responsible purchasing while balancing user welfare and commercial viability.
round1: Describe one or two changes in MirrorAI’s users, clicks or revenue, and show one useful calculation using comparable reporting periods.
round2: Explain the most likely reason for the purchasing pattern, cite released evidence, and name one uncertainty about whether MirrorAI’s design caused it.
round3: Calculate purchasing users before and after the change in your released scenario; state the main assumption about recommendation exposure and purchasing.
round4: Recommend a design or disclosure action; cite evidence, explain the main trade-off between user outcomes and revenue, and name one KPI.
final: After the new evidence, revise your recommendation in the same Round 4 boxes and explain what changed.

name: PrimeEra AI
character: You are Patricia Prime, PrimeEra AI’s CEO. Backed by older investors, your service recommends healthy-aging, grooming and professional-presentation improvements. You want to defend your approach while acknowledging its commercial interests and making fair comparisons.
case: MogTown’s looks economy is booming: sales are rising while profits are falling. The Mayor’s Economic Council has called a hearing. Each team holds different evidence. Use released data and other teams’ reports to explain the problem and recommend what MogTown should do.
goal: Recommend a fair approach to customer wellbeing without treating different customer groups as proof that PrimeEra is better.
round1: Describe one or two features of PrimeEra’s customers or outcomes, and calculate one useful comparison with the public industry dashboard.
round2: Explain the most likely reason PrimeEra’s outcomes differ, cite released evidence, and name one uncertainty about the comparison.
round3: Calculate forecast kept sales under both released return assumptions and their difference; state the main assumption behind your result.
round4: Recommend a company or city action; cite evidence from a fair comparison, explain the main trade-off, and name one KPI.
final: After the new evidence, revise your recommendation in the same Round 4 boxes and explain what changed.

name: CloutHouse
character: You are Chloe Clout, CloutHouse’s director. Your agency connects creators with brands and earns commissions from their campaigns. You want creator marketing to remain valuable while addressing practices that undermine customer trust.
case: MogTown’s looks economy is booming: sales are rising while profits are falling. The Mayor’s Economic Council has called a hearing. Each team holds different evidence. Use released data and other teams’ reports to explain the problem and recommend what MogTown should do.
goal: Recommend how MogTown can preserve useful creator marketing while improving customer outcomes and accountability.
round1: Describe one or two changes in creator sales, commissions or activity, and show one useful calculation from your released dashboard.
round2: Explain the most likely reason campaign outcomes differ, cite released evidence, and name one uncertainty about creators, audiences or products.
round3: Calculate the sales reduction and revised total in your released scenario; state the main assumption linking creator traffic to purchases.
round4: Recommend a creator or campaign policy; cite evidence, explain the main trade-off between channel revenue and customer outcomes, and name one KPI.
final: After the new evidence, revise your recommendation in the same Round 4 boxes and explain what changed.

name: MogTown Consumer Protection Agency
character: You are Carmen Shield, a MogTown Consumer Protection Agency investigator. You examine complaints, refund disputes and advertising claims. You want to prevent consumer harm while using limited enforcement resources where the evidence supports action.
case: MogTown’s looks economy is booming: sales are rising while profits are falling. The Mayor’s Economic Council has called a hearing. Each team holds different evidence. Use released data and other teams’ reports to explain the problem and recommend what MogTown should do.
goal: Recommend targeted protections that reduce preventable harm while considering enforcement capacity and the city’s economy.
round1: Describe one or two changes in complaints or reported concerns, and calculate a useful comparison such as complaints per order.
round2: Explain the most likely cause of a major consumer problem, cite released complaint evidence, and name one uncertainty about that explanation.
round3: Calculate forecast complaints using your released scenario; state the main assumption about complaints per order or reporting behavior.
round4: Choose focused enforcement priorities; cite your evidence, explain the main resource trade-off, and name one KPI for consumer outcomes.
final: After the new evidence, revise your recommendation in the same Round 4 boxes and explain what changed.

name: Mayor’s Economic Council
character: You are Mayor Eli Stone and the Mayor’s Economic Council. You oversee the city’s economic response and hear every organization’s evidence. You want to protect consumers while sustaining jobs, tax revenue and viable businesses.
case: MogTown’s looks economy is booming: sales are rising while profits are falling. The Mayor’s Economic Council has called a hearing. Each team holds different evidence. Use released data and other teams’ reports to explain the problem and recommend what MogTown should do.
goal: Recommend a city response that balances consumer welfare, jobs, tax revenue and financially sustainable businesses.
round1: Describe one or two changes in jobs, taxes, margins or working capital, and show one useful calculation from the released evidence.
round2: Explain the most likely reason industry profit fell, cite released costs and another team’s evidence, and name one uncertainty.
round3: Calculate forecast sales and profit under both released margin assumptions; compare the profits and state the main assumption.
round4: Recommend a targeted city response; cite evidence, explain the main economic and consumer trade-off, and name one KPI to monitor.
final: After the new evidence, revise your recommendation in the same Round 4 boxes and explain what changed.
